prompt: Match each method of `context.Context` with what it gives.
hint: Two of them are about stopping, one about time, one about data.

pairs.right: a channel closed when the work should stop
why it stopped, or nil before
the time it will cancel itself, if any
request-scoped data stored under a key

prompt: In `cancel.go`, `main` cancelled only the parent context. What happened to the worker on the child?
hint: Cancellation travels in one direction in the tree.

choices.text: It kept running until `cancelChild` ran
choices.why: It stopped with the parent; `cancelChild` only runs at the end of `main`.

choices.text: It stopped too, with `context canceled`
choices.why: Right. Cancelling a context cancels all its children.

choices.text: It panicked, because its parent was gone
choices.why: Nothing panics; the child's `Done` closes and its `Err` is set.

choices.text: It stopped with `context deadline exceeded`
choices.why: There is no deadline in `cancel.go`; the reason was a cancel.

prompt: A worker runs a long loop and never looks at `ctx.Done()`. Its owner calls `cancel()`. What happens to the worker?

choices.text: The runtime stops it at the next function call
choices.why: The runtime never stops a goroutine for you; cancellation is a message the goroutine has to read.

choices.text: Nothing: it keeps running until its loop ends
choices.why: Right. A context can only stop code that listens to it.

choices.text: It panics with `context canceled`
choices.why: `context canceled` is a value `Err` returns, not a panic.

choices.text: Its `ctx` is replaced by a fresh one
choices.why: Contexts are immutable; cancelling closes `Done` on the same one.

prompt: The root of every context tree, empty and never cancelled, comes from `context.___()`.
`deadline.go` gave a 300 ms lookup a 100 ms budget. After how long did `lookup` return?

choices.text: 300 ms, with the address
choices.why: It printed `addr ""`: no address, because it gave up.

choices.text: 100 ms, with an empty address
choices.why: Right: `addr "" after 100ms`.

choices.text: 200 ms, the difference between the two
choices.why: The budget is a point in time, not a subtraction.

choices.text: Never, because nothing cancelled it
choices.why: The timeout cancels the context by itself.

hint: What can `Err()` say, and what can it not?

choices.text: `WithTimeout` cannot be cancelled early
choices.why: It can: it returns a `cancel` too.

choices.text: Only `WithTimeoutCause` sets `Err()` to `DeadlineExceeded`
choices.why: Both do; `Err()` printed `context deadline exceeded` as usual.

choices.text: So that `context.Cause` names the budget that ran out
choices.why: Right. `Err()` is one of two values; the cause names the budget.

choices.text: To make the timeout more precise
choices.why: The timing is the same; only the recorded reason differs.

prompt: A request arrives with a context that expires in 2 s. Deep inside, a function calls `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)` for a slow report. When is the new context cancelled?
hint: A child can only tighten a deadline.

choices.text: After 5 s, since the child sets its own
choices.why: A child cannot outlive its parent's deadline.

choices.text: After 2 s
choices.why: Right. The earlier deadline is kept.

choices.text: After 7 s, the two added together
choices.why: Deadlines are points in time; they are not added.

choices.text: Immediately, since 5 s is beyond the parent
choices.why: It is not refused; it just keeps the parent's earlier deadline.

prompt: `go vet` refused `ctx, _ := context.WithTimeout(...)` in `lost.go`. What does an uncalled `cancel` keep alive until the deadline?

choices.text: The goroutine that created the context
choices.why: That goroutine goes on with its life; a context does not hold it.

choices.text: A copy of the whole parent context
choices.why: A child points at its parent; it does not copy it.

choices.text: A timer and a slot in the parent
choices.why: Right. Per request, with long timeouts, those pile up.

choices.text: Nothing: vet's message is about style
choices.why: The message says why: to avoid a context leak.

prompt: Put the lines `deadline.go` printed in order.
hint: It asks about the deadline before it starts the lookup.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson say belongs in a context value?
hint: Data that belongs to the request and crosses API boundaries.

choices.text: The database handle the function needs
choices.why: The function cannot work without it, which makes it a parameter.

choices.text: The id of the request being handled
choices.why: Right: request-scoped, and useful in every log line below.

choices.text: The program's configuration
choices.why: It is the same for every request, so it belongs to the program.

choices.text: An optional flag for one function
choices.why: The documentation says plainly: not for optional parameters.

prompt: In `values.go`, `ctx.Value(0)` returned `<nil>` although the key constant is `0`. Why?
hint: Keys are compared like map keys, type included.

choices.text: Values are looked up by text, not by number
choices.why: Neither: they are compared like map keys. The string `"requestIDKey"` failed as well.

choices.text: The value was stored in a child that `main` cannot see
choices.why: `ctx` is that child; `handle(ctx)` found the id in it.

choices.text: The untyped `0` became an `int`, and the key is a `ctxKey`
choices.why: Right. Different types, different keys, which is the protection.

choices.text: `Value` only works inside `handle`
choices.why: It works anywhere the context is; `main` used the wrong key.

prompt: Two libraries both store a value under the string key `"user"` in the same request's context. What does each see when it reads it back?
hint: `Value` searches from the context outwards to its parents.

choices.text: Whichever value was set nearest to the reading context
choices.why: Right: the nearest match wins, so one library can read the other's value. A private key type prevents it.

choices.text: Each its own value, kept apart by package
choices.why: Nothing separates them: a string key is the same in every package.

choices.text: A panic for a duplicate key
choices.why: `WithValue` accepts any key, duplicates included.

choices.text: `nil`, since the two cancel each other
choices.why: Values do not cancel each other; the nearer one hides the farther.

prompt: Which habits does this lesson recommend? Choose all that apply.
hint: One is about `cancel`, one about errors, one about keys.

choices.text: `defer cancel()` on the line after `WithTimeout`
choices.why: Yes, and `go vet` checks it.

choices.text: Testing for `context.DeadlineExceeded` with `errors.Is`
choices.why: Yes, since callers may wrap the error.

choices.text: An unexported key type for context values
choices.why: Yes, so no other package can collide with it.

choices.text: Letting the worker call `cancel` when it is done
choices.why: The owner cancels; the worker only listens.

prompt: A handler starts a background goroutine that writes an audit record, passing the request's context. The client hangs up. What happens to the audit write, and what does lesson 11 offer for it?
hint: The request's context is cancelled when the request ends.

choices.text: It completes, since background goroutines ignore contexts
choices.why: A goroutine that listens to the request's context stops with it, wherever it runs.

choices.text: It is cancelled too; `WithoutCancel` avoids that
choices.why: Right. The audit is not part of answering, so it needs a context that outlives the request.

choices.text: It panics when the client hangs up
choices.why: Cancellation closes `Done`; it panics nothing.

choices.text: It waits for the client to reconnect
choices.why: Nothing in a context waits for a client.

prompt: Each worker in `cancel.go` takes a step every 30 ms, and `main` cancels after 100 ms. How many steps did each worker report?
